chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Jameel, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who says, “Whatever Allah so Desires, there is neither might nor strength except with Allah,” seventy times, seventy types of afflictions will be averted from him, the least of which is suffocation.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, and what is suffocation?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He will not fall ill with insanity, so he would suffocate.'

key_terms.لَا حَوْلَ وَ لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّ: There is no might and no strength except with Allah (a common dhikr formula)

ai.seo_question: What are the benefits of reciting 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah' seventy times?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), emphasizing the comprehensive protective efficacy of combining the phrase of will ('Ma shaa Allah') with the phrase of power ('La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah'). The promise of warding off seventy afflictions, ranging from physical ailments to mental instability, underscores the Shia scholarly view of this dhikr as a holistic shield against both internal and external trials.
